items.title: Ebonyi residents urged to embrace free family planning
items.description: …As experts lament cultural, religious barriers By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki Residents of Ebonyi State have been urged to take advantage of free family planning services to reduce maternal mortality, unintended pregnancies and unsafe abortions in the state. The call was made as the state joined the rest of the world to commemorate the 2026 World Contraception Day with activities promoting access to family planning and informed reproductive health choices. The week-long activities climaxed with a road walk from Pa Ngele Oruta Township Stadium, Abakaliki, to Eke-Aba Market, where residents were sensitised on making informed and voluntary decisions about their reproductive health. Speaking at the event, the State Coordinator of Family Planning in the Ministry of Health, Mrs Christy Ikechukwu, said this year’s theme, “No Barriers, Just Choices: Contraceptive Access Now,” underscored the need to remove barriers preventing people from accessing contraceptive services. Ikechukwu thanked development partners, including the Johns Hopkins Program for International Education in Gynecology and Obstetrics, JHPIEGO; MSI Nigeria Reproductive Choices; and Prevailing Global Development Initiative, PGDI, for their support. She said family planning services were available free of charge at healthcare centres across the state and encouraged residents to visit the nearest facility to access appropriate services. Ikechukwu commended the state government’s efforts in the health sector and praised the Commissioner for Health, Dr Moses Ekuma, for deploying adequate manpower to health facilities across the state. She said the measure had contributed to increased uptake of family planning services, particularly in rural communities. According to her, “contraception saves lives and transforms the future.” “I enjoin government, development partners, and community leaders to strengthen investments in reproductive health and ensure no woman of child-bearing age is left behind,” she said. She also dismissed misconceptions about contraceptive side effects and urged men to support their partners in accessing accurate information and appropriate reproductive health services. The MSI Regional Manager, South, Mrs Ogoamaka Aginam, said child spacing could contribute to reducing maternal and neonatal deaths. She said proper family planning could also improve household welfare and contribute to healthier communities. “When families plan properly, communities thrive, poverty declines and the cycle of ill health is broken,” she said. Aginam, however, lamented cultural and religious barriers that continued to hinder access to family planning services and urged women, irrespective of age or marital status, to consider contraception as part of efforts to protect their health and that of their children. Also speaking, the Family Planning Supervisor, Ohaukwu Local Government Area, Mrs Okpaga Mary, and her Ezza South counterpart, Mrs Eleke Jacinta, said the global campaign was aimed at promoting a world where every pregnancy was wanted. They noted that unintended pregnancies could contribute to preventable maternal deaths, stressing the importance of access to accurate information and voluntary family planning services. The post Ebonyi residents urged to embrace free family planning appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Two reportedly die after being trapped in mining pit at Juaboso
items.description: Two people have died following an incident at a mining site in Juaboso in the Juaboso District of the Western North Region. According to 3News, two men reportedly entered the mining pit around noon on Saturday, September 26, 2026, to mine but later became weak underground. Preliminary reports indicate the pair may have struggled with excessive heat and inadequate ventilation inside the pit. When they failed to return by the morning of Sunday, September 27, a friend reportedly went into the pit to find out what had happened. The friend is said to have discovered the two men in a weakened condition and raised the alarm, prompting residents and other community members to organise a rescue effort. The victims were subsequently removed from the pit and rushed to the Juaboso Government Hospital, where medical personnel pronounced them dead. One of the deceased has been identified as Richard Oduro, popularly known as “Churches”, a resident of Juaboso Township. The identity of the second victim, who is believed to be from outside the community, has not yet been established. Authorities have yet to officially determine the circumstances surrounding the incident and the exact cause of the two deaths.

items.title: Atiku asks Tinubu to explain rising debt
items.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to explain the continued rise in Nigeria’s public debt despite increased government revenues, saying Nigerians are yet to see the benefits promised from the administration’s economic reforms. Atiku, who is the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, made the demand in a statement issued on Saturday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communications of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council. His comments followed the latest figures from the Debt Management Office, DMO, which put Nigeria’s total public debt at ₦166.79 trillion as of June 30, 2026. The DMO figure represents an increase from ₦159.35 trillion recorded as of March 31, 2026. Atiku said the government had removed petrol subsidy, increased its revenues and continued borrowing, while Nigerians were facing higher costs of food, transportation, energy and other essential needs. “A government that says more money is coming in must explain why it keeps borrowing and why the people paying for its policies cannot see the promised gains,” he said. He said Nigeria’s public debt had risen from ₦49.85 trillion in March 2023 to ₦166.79 trillion by June 2026, citing DMO figures. Atiku called on the President to provide a detailed breakdown of the country’s debt profile, including old debts newly recorded, the impact of exchange-rate changes on foreign-denominated debt and all new loans contracted since the administration came into office. “I expect President Tinubu to put the full account before Nigerians,” he said. “He should identify the old debt newly recorded, the foreign debt whose naira value rose with the exchange rate, and every new loan contracted since he assumed office.” The former Vice-President also requested details of the amount of debt already repaid and the outstanding balance. “Accounting explanations must not become a hiding place for fresh borrowing,” he said. ‘Economy producing two Nigerias’ Atiku said the country’s debt situation should be considered alongside what he described as a widening gap between reported improvements in macroeconomic indicators and the experiences of ordinary Nigerians. “The Tinubu economy is producing two Nigerias: one in which ordinary citizens are suffocating under rising food, fuel, transport, electricity, education and housing costs, and another in which those with wealth, access and privilege are far better positioned to protect and multiply their fortunes,” he said. He argued that improvements in government revenue, foreign reserves and other macroeconomic indicators should not, on their own, be treated as sufficient evidence of economic success if many Nigerians continue to struggle to afford basic necessities. “The true test of economic policy is whether Nigerians can afford food, transportation, housing, education, healthcare and electricity,” Atiku said. He also referred to a June 2026 assessment by the International Monetary Fund, IMF, which acknowledged improvements in Nigeria’s macroeconomic performance following reforms but noted that conditions remained difficult for many Nigerians. The IMF also estimated significant levels of poverty and food insecurity in the country. Atiku further cited prevailing petrol and diesel prices, arguing that higher energy costs had increased pressure on household budgets. “The philosophy of an economic reform cannot be that the poor surrender more and more while those already insulated from hardship become increasingly comfortable,” he said. “Nigerians were promised that today’s pain would produce tomorrow’s gain. After more than three years, they are entitled to ask: gain for whom?” Atiku questions debt servicing The former Vice-President also raised concerns about the proportion of government revenue being used to service debt. He cited BudgIT figures showing that debt service reached ₦12.52 trillion in the third quarter of 2025, compared with revenue of ₦18.63 trillion. “Money committed to debt service is money unavailable for competing public needs,” Atiku said. “Nigerians were told to endure the pain because there would be gains. Where are those gains?” He also referred to the 2026 fiscal framework, which provides for about ₦68.32 trillion in expenditure against projected revenue of ₦36.87 trillion, leaving a projected deficit of about ₦31.45 trillion. Atiku said President Tinubu’s reported remarks at the Africa Forward Summit in Nairobi in May, where the President put Nigeria’s 2026 debt-service bill at about $11.6 billion, illustrated the pressure created by debt repayments. “If President Tinubu understands abroad what debt payments are taking away from Nigeria, then he must explain at home why the borrowing bill continues to grow,” he said. Atiku warned that fiscal pressure could worsen when borrowing becomes routine, debt service takes up an increasing share of government revenue and governments repeatedly borrow to finance budget deficits. The post Atiku asks Tinubu to explain rising debt appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Rencontre Lavrov-Wadephul à l'ONU : Zakharova dénonce une manœuvre politique pour sauver la cote de Merz
items.description: Les negociations entre le ministre russe des Affaires etrangeres, Sergueï Lavrov, et son homologue allemand, Johann Wadephul, sollicitees par la partie allemande, n'etaient liees qu'a la situation politique interieure du pays, a declare la porte-parole du ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres, Maria Zakharova, lors de l'emission « Dimanche soir avec Vladimir Soloviov ». Selon elle, l'initiative du ministre visait a faire preuve d'activite diplomatique aux yeux du peuple allemand. Maria Zakharova a egalement ajoute que Berlin poursuivait un autre objectif avec cette rencontre : redresser d'une maniere ou d'une autre la cote de popularite en baisse du chancelier allemand Friedrich Merz. Moscou n'a « rien tire de nouveau » La rencontre entre Sergueï Lavrov et Johann Wadephul a eu lieu le 26 septembre en marge de l'Assemblee generale des Nations unies a New York. Il s'agissait de la premiere rencontre diplomatique entre la Russie et l'Allemagne depuis 2022, et elle n'a dure qu'une vingtaine de minutes. Selon Maria Zakharova, les representants du ministere allemand des Affaires etrangeres ont exige de limiter la presence des journalistes, d'exclure les questions de la presse et de ne pas publier d'articles avant la fin des negociations. Toutefois, ce n'est pas un hasard si la discussion a ete si breve. Commentant cette rencontre lors de sa conference de presse de cloture , Sergueï Lavrov a fait remarquer qu'il n'avait « rien tire de nouveau » de la part de son homologue allemand : « Il a sorti des notes et a lu un texte qui reprenait integralement ce que l'Allemagne, par la voix de ses dirigeants, declare officiellement et publiquement chaque jour. » Wadephul a « honteusement couvert » le rapport sur les falsifications a Boutcha Le chef de la diplomatie russe a ajoute que la presentation allemande laissait transparaître un sous-entendu selon lequel Berlin a « consenti a entrer en contact » avec Moscou et que, desormais, en echange de « ce geste de bonne volonte », la partie russe devrait faire des « concessions sur le front ukrainien ». Johann Wadephul a egalement formule des reproches concernant un drone decouvert a Leipzig, affirmant que la partie allemande avait juge « tres probable » qu'il soit d'origine russe, sans presenter de preuves a Moscou, a poursuivi Sergueï Lavrov. En reponse, le chef de la diplomatie russe lui a conseille de relire son intervention au Conseil de securite sur l'Ukraine, le 23 septembre. a l'issue de la reunion, Maria Zakharova a egalement fait part de ses commentaires, indiquant que, pendant les negociations, un rapport du Tribunal public international sur les crimes des neonazis ukrainiens concernant la mise en scene a Boutcha, intitule « Les heritiers de Goebbels », se trouvait sur la table. Selon elle, Johann Wadephul « a honteusement couvert le rapport avec un carnet et a fait semblant de ne rien remarquer », comme si la comparaison avec Goebbels ne les concernait pas. « Mais c'est evident pour tout le monde et seule la verite fait mal », a-t-elle souligne.

items.title: UK police arrest 5 after 'major incident' at Fairford airbase used by US air forces
items.description: British counter-terrorism police were on Sunday probing a “major” incident near a base used by the US air force after arresting five men on suspicion of “preparing a terrorist act”, police said. In March, then prime minister Keir Starmer granted permission for “defensive” US action against Iranian missile sites from two UK bases including Fairford. Armed officers detained the group in the early hours of Sunday after a call to emergency services about three “suspicious vehicles which appeared to be travelling towards the airbase”, London’s Metropolitan Police said in a statement . The suspects were initially held near the Royal Air Force (RAF) Fairford air base in Gloucestershire, southwest England, on suspicion of explosives offences. Some 85 households in the nearby village of Whelford were advised to evacuate and army bomb disposal experts were called in to examine three vans stopped on a rural road. “Counter Terrorism Policing can now confirm they are leading an investigation into an incident which took place overnight near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire,” the Met statement added. Broadcast aerial footage showed a bomb disposal robot on a rural road moving around the vans, two of which had their rear doors open. Police believed the incident had been “contained” and a 400-metre cordon had been put in place. Armed officers could be seen guarding the entrance to the base. Prime Minister Andy Burnham was being kept updated on the incident, a government spokesperson said. “We are grateful to the emergency services, who have acted quickly to detain several suspects and put measures in place to keep the community safe,” the spokesperson said. “It would be inappropriate to comment further whilst investigations are ongoing.” Defence Minister Wes Streeting thanked “emergency and specialist teams” deployed to the scene. “We can be reassured that this is being dealt with,” he said on X. Gloucestershire Police said earlier it had declared a “major incident” with several men arrested “on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act”. Villagers evacuated Residents were evacuated to a nearby leisure centre, police said. Villager Julian Tudsbery said he was woken and advised to leave at about 7am (11am PKT) by police “banging on the door”. He said a fellow villager had alerted police in the middle of the night after spotting the vans. “They phoned the airbase police, who didn’t answer the phone. It just rang out so she dialled 999,” he told the BBC . Fairford is the UK base of the 501st Combat Support Wing, a US air force administrative support wing, which said in a statement that no US air force personnel had been involved in the incident. “The 501st Combat Support Wing appreciates the swift response and continued support of our local law enforcement partners,” it said. “We remain in close coordination with our UK partners to help ensure the safety and security of both our military and local communities,” it added. The MP for the area, Roz Savage, described the situation as “worrying”. “I have contacted the police for further updates and I’ve been told that it is believed the incident is contained,” she said on X. The incident comes amid concerns about the actions of hostile foreign states. Interior Minister Shabana Mahmood has accused Iran and Russia of using proxies to carry out criminal activities on their behalf on UK territory. Earlier this month, reports said British military sites had been targeted by drones more than 300 times over the past year. Britain’s defence ministry did not disclose who was behind the drone activity, but the figures come as European countries have warned of an increase in suspected Russian hybrid operations on their territory. Russia denies mounting hybrid attacks on Western nations. Britain said in July its armed forces were ready to protect the country from any attack after Iran’s Revolutionary Guards issued a warning not to allow US bombers to fly from Fairford.

items.title: Petrosol cleans up Wa Municipal Hospital, to donate medical equipment
items.description: Petrosol Platinum Energy PLC has embarked on a clean-up exercise at the Wa Municipal Hospital as part of its annual Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative, with plans to donate medical equipment to the facility on Monday, September 28. The exercise saw staff of Petrosol and volunteers cut down overgrown weeds, desilt choked drains and clear bushy areas that had become breeding grounds for snakes and rodents. Hospital authorities said the intervention was long overdue. Due to the hospital’s large compound and limited number of casual workers, weeds had taken over parts of the facility, with reports of snakes entering some wards and administrative offices. The clean-up exercise, however, is only the first phase of the company’s intervention. Speaking to JoyNews Upper West Regional Correspondent, Rafiq Salam, the Head of Marketing at Petrosol Platinum Energy PLC, Philip Buama Asampong, said the company would return on Monday to donate medical equipment to the hospital. “We are not just doing weeding and cleaning, but we are going beyond the clean-up exercise. The hospital needs a lot of equipment to work with. We are going to also donate medical equipment to the hospital tomorrow to support the good work that government and other stakeholders are doing,” he said. He explained that with 109 service stations nationwide, 41 percent of which are located in northern Ghana, the company had a responsibility to give back to the communities in which it operates. “Our theme for this year is ‘Energizing Dreams’. We want to energise the dreams of the community we do business with. Health is a core need of every human being,” Mr Asampong added. The Medical Superintendent of the Wa Municipal Hospital, Dr Bukari Zakari, described the intervention as heartwarming, revealing that the hospital had recently appealed for support on radio. “A healthy environment is a healthy human being. We invest a lot in casuals to clean the environment, so if Petrosol sees it necessary to do this for us, we are indeed very grateful. We didn’t even send a proposal — they open-heartedly presented themselves to do this donation. It will go a long way to improve service delivery,” he said. Petrosol Platinum Energy PLC said it remained committed to supporting communities where it operates, with the Wa Municipal Hospital being the latest beneficiary of its “Energizing Dreams” CSR initiative.

items.title: Oyebanji dissolves boards, sacks political appointees
items.description: Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, has approved the immediate dissolution of boards, commissions and parastatals in the state and terminated the appointments of all political appointees. Those affected by the termination include Special Assistants, Senior Special Assistants and Technical Assistants. The decision was contained in a statement issued on Sunday by the Governor’s Special Adviser on Media, Yinka Oyebode. According to the statement, the decision became necessary as the governor’s first term gradually winds down ahead of the inauguration of his second term scheduled for October 16, 2026. However, chairmen and members of statutory boards are exempted from the dissolution. They include the State Independent Electoral Commission, SIEC; Civil Service Commission; House of Assembly Service Commission; and Judicial Service Commission. The governing councils of all state-owned tertiary institutions will also remain intact, in line with earlier directives by the governor. The chairmen of the State Universal Basic Education Board, SUBEB; Local Government Service Commission; and Teaching Service Commission will remain in office, although the respective boards have been dissolved. Also exempted from the termination of appointments are Directors-General and Technical Advisers to the governor. Oyebanji expressed appreciation to the affected appointees for their contributions to the success of his administration and their service to the state. He wished them continued success in their future endeavours. The post Oyebanji dissolves boards, sacks political appointees appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Terrorists abduct newlywed couple, four others in Kwara
items.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin A newlywed couple, identified as Funmilayo Bamidele and her husband, Reverend Abiodun David, and four others have reportedly been abducted along the Eruku-Iyemero Road bordering Kwara and Kogi states. The victims were reportedly abducted on Saturday evening while returning from their engagement ceremony in Eruku, Kwara State. Vanguard gathered from sources that the group was travelling in a vehicle expected to take the Isanlu Road when the driver reportedly opted for a back route to drop off the Best Man and other members of the group in Iyamoye, Kogi State. The vehicle was reportedly intercepted by suspected terrorists along the Iyemero-Eruku Road, where the occupants were abducted. Further details about the incident, including the whereabouts of the other victims and efforts to secure their release, were still being awaited as of Sunday. Confirming the incident, the Kwara State Commissioner of Police, Adekimi Ojo, said security operatives had launched a joint rescue operation to locate the victims and apprehend the perpetrators. Ojo said soldiers were already combing the bush in an effort to rescue the abducted persons. He also disclosed that the vehicle in which the victims were travelling had been found parked at an abandoned police station in Ayetoro, Ekiti State. The commissioner added that police operatives in Kwara, Kogi and Ekiti states were working together on the rescue operation because the incident occurred around the border communities of the three states. items.title: Maroc-Gabon : trop subir, trop peu menacer, les Panthères battues d’entrée
items.description: La première de Sébastien Migné sur le banc gabonais s’est heurtée à la maîtrise marocaine. Battues 2-0 par les Lions de l’Atlas, le 25 septembre au stade Prince Moulay Abdellah de Rabat, les Panthères ont manqué leur entrée dans les éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. Privées notamment de Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang et de Mario Lemina, elles ont trop longtemps subi pour espérer mieux. Dès le 29 septembre, face au Niger à Franceville, une réaction sera attendue. Les Panthères du Gabon ont débuté leur campagne qualificative pour la CAN 2027 par une défaite (2 à 0), face aux Lions de l’Atlas du Maroc. © D.R. Les Panthères du Gabon ont ouvert leur campagne de qualification pour la Coupe d’Afrique des nations (CAN) 2027 par une défaite face au Maroc (2-0), à Rabat. Pour sa première rencontre à la tête de la sélection, Sébastien Migné avait opté pour un 4-3-3, avec une charnière centrale inédite composée de Michel Mboula et de Jonathan Do Marcolino. Dans un match largement contrôlé par les Lions de l’Atlas, le Gabon a payé son manque d’efficacité et ses fragilités défensives, malgré quelques occasions de revenir au score. Le Maroc a rapidement imposé son rythme. Azzedine Ounahi a d’abord trouvé la barre à la 27ᵉ minute, avant que Noussair Mazraoui n’ouvre le score à la 36ᵉ, d’une frappe puissante. Longtemps acculées en défense, les Panthères ont toutefois montré des signes de réveil après la pause, notamment par Denis Bouanga, dont deux tentatives ont été repoussées par Yassine Bounou. « Les Panthères se sont contentées de limiter la casse », a résumé un supporter de la sélection gabonaise. Le Maroc a scellé sa victoire en fin de rencontre. Entré en jeu, Soufiane Rahimi a inscrit le second but à la 84ᵉ minute, sur un service de Bilal El Khannouss. Malgré quelques séquences offensives, les hommes de Migné n’ont pu inverser la tendance. Dans le groupe A, le Niger, vainqueur du Lesotho (2-1), rejoint le Maroc en tête. Les Panthères devront réagir dès le mardi 29 septembre, à Franceville, face au Mena du Niger, pour prendre leurs premiers points et lancer leur campagne qualificative. L’article Maroc-Gabon : trop subir, trop peu menacer, les Panthères battues d’entrée est apparu en premier sur Gabonreview.com | Actualité du Gabon | .

items.title: Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 27 dead
items.description: JOHANNESBURG — At least 27 people have been killed in two separate mass shootings in South Africa, hours apart, in the latest incidents of gun violence to hit the country. Seventeen people were killed when eight gunmen reportedly stormed a bar near Johannesburg on Saturday evening, while 15 others were injured. In a separate incident in the early hours of Sunday, 10 people were killed outside an entertainment venue in a township near Cape Town, with 11 others injured. Police had not established a definitive motive for either attack as of Sunday morning, while no arrests had been reported. In Johannesburg, the gunmen opened fire on customers outside the bar before continuing the attack inside. They also reportedly set two vehicles on fire before fleeing the scene. Police said 13 men and four women were killed in the attack. Gauteng Police Commissioner, Lt. Gen. Tommy Mthombeni, said nationals of Ethiopia and Lesotho were among those caught up in the shooting, although the majority of the victims were South African. He said police believed robbery could have been the motive, as personal belongings were reportedly taken, but added that investigators had not ruled out turf wars involving illegal mining groups. Illegal mining in abandoned shafts and dump sites remains a persistent problem in South Africa, with authorities saying undocumented migrants are often recruited by organised crime gangs to carry out the activities. Earlier, the Deputy Provincial Police Commissioner, Maj. Gen. Fred Kekana, told news agency AFP that the Johannesburg attack could have been retaliation for an incident last month in which one person was killed and another injured. Kekana said police had clear images of some of the suspects and, in some cases, their names. In Cape Town, five victims died at the scene, while another five died after being taken to hospital. The shootings came days after 11 people were killed in Durban when gunmen reportedly stormed a house in the KwaMakhutha township. South Africa has one of the highest murder rates in the world and has struggled for years with gun violence, much of it linked to organised crime and gang activity. About 60 murders are recorded daily in the country, which has a population of about 62 million, according to official figures cited in reports on the country’s security situation. The recent spate of mass shootings has heightened concerns over the spread of organised gun violence, with authorities linking some attacks to turf wars between gangs involved in drug trafficking and illegal mining. In February, President Cyril Ramaphosa described organised crime as “the most immediate threat to our democracy, our society and our economic development”. Earlier this year, the military was deployed alongside the police in areas with some of the country’s highest murder rates as part of efforts to curb armed violence. Meanwhile, police in Ekurhuleni, east of Johannesburg, said on Saturday that they had found the body of a 10th woman in an area where a series of similar deaths had been recorded. Local police said they could not rule out the possibility that a serial killer was operating in the area. BBC The post Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 27 dead appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Dattes : l’Algérie exporte plus que la Tunisie, mais gagne moins de devises
items.description: Il y a comme un paradoxe dans les exportations de la filière algérienne des dattes. L'Algérie exporte plus que la Tunisie mais engrange nettement moins de devises que son voisin de l’Est. La datte algérienne , réputée être l’une des meilleures au monde, est-elle bradée ? La datte algérienne exportée pour une moyenne de 993 dollars la tonne Selon un classement établi par l'agence Ecofin à partir des données de la plateforme Trade Map, l'Algérie est le premier exportateur africain de dattes avec un volume d'exportation qui s’est élevé en 2025 à 185 000 tonnes. Le montant des recettes tirées de ces exportations est de 184 millions de dollars, soit moins de 1 dollar par kilogramme. Aussi, l'Algérie n’exporte qu'une petite partie de sa production estimée en 2024 par l'Organisation des Nations unies pour l’alimentation et l’agriculture (FAO) à 1,34 millions de tonnes sur une superficie de 176 000 hectares de palmeraies. La Tunisie vend moins que l’Algérie mais engrange plus Le deuxième exportateur africain c'est la Tunisie avec 147 000 tonnes de dattes (160 000 selon le Groupement interprofessionnel des dattes tunisien) expédiées vers les marchés mondiaux en 2025. Avec 38 000 tonnes de moins, la Tunisie a engrangé près du double des recettes de l’Algérie, soit 347 millions de dinars. Cet écart s'explique par la différence des prix appliqués par les exportateurs des deux pays. Selon les données de Trade Map, les dattes tunisiennes sont exportées en moyenne pour 2 000 dollars la tonne, contre seulement 993 $ la tonne pour les dattes algériennes. Ces prix font de la Tunisie un des principaux exportateurs mondiaux et le premier en Afrique en valeur, s'accaparant 13 % du marché mondial. En production, la Tunisie est loin derrière l’Algérie, avec 400 219 tonnes de dattes produites en 2024, sur une superficie de 81 732 hectares de palmeraies. La datte égyptienne est la plus rentable en Afrique Le premier producteur du continent c'est l’Égypte (1,75 millions de tonnes) mais ce pays n’est que troisième en termes d’exportation (39 000 tonnes en 2025). La datte égyptienne est aussi plus rentable à l’exportation que celle en provenance d'Algérie, et même par rapport à celle de Tunisie. Les 39 000 tonnes exportées en 2025 par l’Égypte ont rapporté 147 millions de dollars, soit une moyenne de 3700 dollars par tonne. Le top 5 africain des exportateurs de dattes est complété par la Libye avec 16 000 tonnes et 25 millions de dollars de recettes et l'Afrique du Sud (6000 tonnes, 26 millions USD de revenus). items.title: Tinubu celebrates Bishop Oyedepo at 72
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has congratulated the Founder and Presiding Bishop of Living Faith Church Worldwide, Bishop David Olaniyi Oyedepo, on his 72nd birthday. President Tinubu said he joined the Oyedepo family, Living Faith Church Worldwide, the Christian community and millions of Bishop Oyedepo’s admirers i”n celebrating a life devoted to faith, service, leadership and human development.” A statement by the presidential spokesman, Bayo Onanuga stated that the President acknowledged Bishop Oyedepo’s remarkable contributions to the moral and spiritual development of individuals and communities, particularly his consistent emphasis on integrity, discipline, diligence, responsibility and excellence. He noted the Bishop’s longstanding advocacy for values that strengthen families, institutions, and nations, and his message of hope, purpose, and personal responsibility, which has resonated with people across Nigeria and beyond. President Tinubu commended Bishop Oyedepo’s significant contributions to education and human-capital development through institutions such as Covenant University and Landmark University, which have provided platforms for academic excellence, leadership development, entrepreneurship and innovation. He said: “Bishop Oyedepo’s influence extends beyond the pulpit into education, publishing, leadership development and humanitarian service, with the Living Faith Church maintaining a significant international presence across Africa and other parts of the world. “For over four decades of ministry, Bishop Oyedepo has become a prominent Nigerian voice on faith, leadership, integrity, education and human development, with his books and teachings reaching audiences across national and continental boundaries. “Bishop David Oyedepo has devoted decades to preaching faith, promoting integrity and encouraging excellence, while investing substantially in education and the development of human capacity. His commitment to building lives, institutions and communities has given his ministry a significant national and international footprint. “I especially salute Bishop Oyedepo for the social-development initiatives, including schools, healthcare facilities, and humanitarian interventions, associated with his ministry and the David Oyedepo Foundation’s support for education and people in need. “On this auspicious occasion of his 72nd birthday, I celebrate his life of service and pray that Almighty God will continue to grant him wisdom, strength, good health and renewed grace as he advances the cause of faith, education, morality and human development. “I wish Bishop Oyedepo many more years of fulfilment, good health and continued service to God and humanity,” Tinubu added. items.title: Lagos traffic is lifestyle, not problem — Hamzat
items.description: Lagos State Deputy Governor, Obafemi Hamzat, has described the state’s perennial traffic congestion as a “lifestyle” that has become part of the identity of the megacity. Hamzat spoke on Saturday at Podfest Naija, a gathering of storytellers and creatives, where he discussed how Lagos’ traffic, crowds and chaotic character had influenced the city’s creative industry. According to him, the hours Lagosians spend in traffic have inadvertently created an audience for podcasters and other digital content creators. “Anyone who has crossed Third Mainland Bridge at 6pm knows that Lagos traffic is not the problem, it is just a lifestyle,” Hamzat said. “In fact, I suspect that many of us in this room, we produce things that are consumed, episode by episode, between Ojota and Obalende. “So in a way, traffic has been a patron of your industry. So you must celebrate traffic. That’s why we are Lagos.” Hamzat said Lagos’ unique character had inspired generations of artists, writers, filmmakers and other creatives. He noted that the narrative about Lagos, which was previously shaped largely by outsiders, was increasingly being told by the city’s own creative community. “Lagos is now telling its own story and the people telling it in a very serious way are in this room,” he said. “The podcasters, the filmmakers, the musician, writer, designers, developers and entrepreneurs who have turned Lagos microphone into a global broadcast.” Creatives need sustainable business models The deputy governor urged creatives to develop sustainable business models, warning that a large audience alone did not guarantee commercial success. He said the state was supporting the creative and innovation ecosystem by funding ideas and research projects. “So we’re funding ideas, not just applauding them. Lagos is supporting nothing less than 90 research and development projects,” he said. “Gone are the years of great ideas and no funding. “A podcast with a million listeners and no business model is just a hobby with good microphone.” Hamzat also stressed the importance of safety and liberty to the creative process, saying people needed to feel secure before they could freely create and tell stories. “Creativity flourishes best when people feel safe,” he said. “For us in Lagos, safety and liberty guarantees remain a matter of right.” Hamzat, who is the All Progressives Congress, APC, governorship candidate in Lagos State for the 2027 general election, said Lagos was currently the safest state in the country, adding that maintaining the situation came at a “ridiculous cost”. “Lagos is today the safest state in our country and it comes at ridiculous cost because if we’re not safe then we can’t even tell stories,” he said. The deputy governor also urged Nigerians to reconnect with their culture, arguing that cultural identity remained important to the country’s development. “One of the challenges for us as Africans, as black people, is that we have forgotten our culture,” he said. “The truth is, we will not prosper — it’s not a curse — if we don’t deal with our culture.” The post Lagos traffic is lifestyle, not problem — Hamzat appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘If NPP was ‘insensitive’ over fuel prices, NDC must accept same description now’ — Amin Adam
items.description: Former Finance Minister and Ranking Member on Parliament’s Finance Committee, Dr Mohammed Amin Adam, has challenged the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) to accept the same description it used against the former New Patriotic Party (NPP) government over rising fuel prices, arguing that the economic circumstances being cited to explain current increases also existed under the previous administration. In a Facebook post on Sunday, September 27, Dr Amin Adam said the NDC, while in opposition, repeatedly described rising fuel prices under the then Akufo-Addo/Bawumia administration as evidence of “insensitive and bad leadership”. He said the party blamed taxes, cedi depreciation and economic management for the increases and demanded that the government stabilise the currency to bring down fuel prices. Dr Amin Adam, however, noted that the 2021 increases occurred amid a major global energy shock, with Brent crude rising from about US$50 per barrel at the beginning of the year to approximately US$86 by late October. He also cited US Energy Information Administration data showing that global petroleum inventories fell by 469 million barrels in 2021, while the IMF reported that Brent had risen above US$85 amid tight energy supplies and a global surge in energy prices. “The fuel pump has a long memory,” Dr Amin Adam wrote, arguing that the economic principles governing fuel prices have not changed simply because there has been a change in government. “The economics has always been straightforward: International product price × Exchange rate + Taxes/Levies + Margins = Domestic Pump Price,” he stated, stressing that Ghana remains largely a price-taker in the international petroleum market and that movements in global prices and the exchange rate affect domestic pump prices. He therefore argued that the standard applied by the NDC to the former NPP government over rising fuel prices should also be applied to the NDC government now in office. “If the NPP was insensitive and provided bad leadership because fuel prices were rising, then the NDC should accept the same description now, rather than trying so hard to explain it away,” he said. According to Dr Amin Adam, the international petroleum prices, geopolitical pressures and exchange-rate dynamics being cited by the NDC today were also factors in 2021. “The fuel pump has not changed the economics. It has simply changed who has to explain it,” he added.

items.title: Cataracte, soins dentaires, circoncisions : sur 3 jours à Libreville, le Samu social lève la barrière du coût
items.description: Chirurgie de la cataracte, circoncisions et soins dentaires : à Libreville, le Samu social a consacré trois journées à des interventions gratuites, du 24 au 26 septembre. Cette campagne succède à une opération menée à Port-Gentil, où la structure annonce 9 029 prises en charge. Deux mobilisations pour rendre les soins accessibles à ceux que leur coût peut en éloigner. Un moment des consultations à Libreville. © Samu social Le Samu social de Libreville a achevé, samedi 26 septembre, une campagne de prise en charge médicale gratuite lancée le jeudi 24 septembre. Pendant trois jours, l’opération a proposé aux populations plusieurs prestations, dans la continuité de son action en faveur de l’accès aux soins. La campagne comprenait notamment des opérations de la cataracte, des circoncisions et des actes de médecine bucco-dentaire : soins dentaires, extractions et détartrages. Cette mobilisation est venue compléter les prestations habituellement assurées sans frais par le Samu social. Selon la structure, la médecine générale, la radiologie et les bilans sanguins restent accessibles gratuitement 24 heures sur 24. Le numéro 1488 permet également de joindre ses services. 9 029 prises en charge annoncées à Port-Gentil Cette campagne intervient quelques jours après une opération menée à Port-Gentil, au cours de laquelle 9 029 prises en charge ont été enregistrées, selon les données communiquées par la structure. Présenté comme historique par le Samu social, ce bilan illustre l’importance du recours à ces prestations gratuites. À Libreville, les trois journées de mobilisation ont permis de proposer différents soins sans frais, notamment aux personnes confrontées à des difficultés financières. Aucun bilan chiffré de cette campagne n’est toutefois précisé dans les éléments communiqués. Au-delà de ces opérations ponctuelles, l’enjeu reste celui de la continuité : permettre aux personnes qui en ont besoin d’accéder durablement aux soins essentiels. items.title: Igbo group urges Soludo, Obi to sheathe swords
items.description: By Emmanuel Iheaka The Igbo Heroes and Icons Foundation has called for a truce between the Anambra State Government and the candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, amid disagreements over the state’s loans and financial obligations. In a statement endorsed by its National Coordinator, Hon. Chinedu Nsofor, the group appealed to both sides to embrace peace and collaboration in the interest of the Igbo people’s aspiration for the presidency. There has been a disagreement between Governor Chukwuma Soludo’s administration and Obi over loans and debts which the Anambra State Government said were incurred by the administration of the former governor. The foundation said there could be constructive disagreement without denigrating Obi’s political standing or Soludo’s position as governor of Anambra State. It maintained that the dispute over the loans and other financial obligations should be resolved through an unbiased examination of documentary evidence rather than verbal attacks and counter-attacks. “The foundation’s position is that whatever political differences may exist between the two prominent sons of Anambra, those differences should not become a permanent source of division among Ndigbo. “The foundation is particularly concerned about the continuing controversy surrounding claims about loans and other financial obligations allegedly inherited by successive administrations from the administration of former Governor Peter Obi. This is an issue that should be settled by documentary evidence rather than political exchanges,” it said. The group said every government had a legitimate responsibility to account for public resources inherited from previous administrations. “Governor Soludo, as the incumbent Governor of Anambra State, has the right to examine previous financial records and explain the state’s fiscal position to the people. Similarly, former Governor Peter Obi has the right to respond to allegations concerning the record of his administration. “Neither accountability nor criticism should be interpreted as hostility. But accountability is most credible when it is supported by verifiable records,” the foundation said. It urged the parties to avoid allowing the dispute to undermine what it described as the Igbo aspiration to produce the next president of Nigeria in line with equity and justice. The foundation also called on Igbo political leaders, professionals, traditional institutions, religious leaders, youths, business leaders and civil society organisations to approach the question of an Igbo presidency with maturity. “The goal should not be to silence disagreement. The goal should be to make disagreement constructive. The goal should not be to force every Igbo person into one political party. “Ndigbo can belong to different political parties and still discuss shared interests. They can support different candidates and still cooperate on development. They can disagree about Peter Obi and still respect him. They can disagree with Soludo and still respect the office of the Governor of Anambra State,” the group said. items.title: Man allegedly stabs friend to death over ₦500 in Cross River
items.description: Mob attacks police station, demands suspect’s releas e By Emma Una CALABAR — A man identified as Ebino Mbang Ikpi has been arrested by the police in Cross River State for allegedly stabbing his friend, Ayei Ekpe Ibor, 42, to death following a disagreement over the sharing of ₦500 reportedly given to both of them as a gift. The incident occurred on Saturday afternoon at Kekoti, Ajere, in Yakurr Local Government Area of the state. The state Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Sunday Eitokpah, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday. According to him, the police received a report that a man had been stabbed to death following an alleged misunderstanding between the victim and his friend, Ikpi. “We got a report that a man had been stabbed to death on Saturday afternoon at Kekoti, Ajere, following an alleged misunderstanding with his friend, Ebino Mbang Ikpi, male, of Kekoti, Ajere. “The misunderstanding was reportedly over ₦500 said to have been given as a gift to both men, which allegedly resulted in a fight,” he said. Eitokpah said Ibor was confirmed dead following the attack, while the suspect fled the scene. He said police operatives immediately commenced efforts to locate the suspect and arrested him at about 8:40 a.m. in his hideout in the Ajere-Ekori area. “He was subsequently taken to Yakurr Division for detention and further investigation,” the police spokesman said. However, shortly after the arrest, some sympathisers and other persons allegedly mobilised and attacked the Ekori Police Division, demanding the release of the suspect. Eitokpah said the group, upon discovering that the suspect was not at the station, allegedly resorted to throwing stones at the facility. He said the attack resulted in damage to seven windows, the DPO/DCO office door, six plastic chairs, a wall mirror, part of the roofing and the passenger-side glass of the DPO’s official vehicle. The residence of the Ajere Youth Leader, Omini Jacob, was also allegedly attacked over claims that he had assisted the police. The police spokesman said operatives responded promptly, dispersed the mob and restored normalcy. He added that the situation had been brought under control and the police station reinforced with additional security. The Commissioner of Police in Cross River State, CP Ajo Geoffrey Ordue, has directed that the suspect be transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department, SCID, for further investigation. He also directed intensified efforts to identify and arrest all persons allegedly involved in the attack and destruction of police and private property. items.title: No govt financing, sovereign-guaranteed loans for new PIA aircraft: adviser to finmin
items.description: Adviser to the Finance Minister Khurram Schehzad clarified on Sunday that the government was not buying any aircraft for Pakistan International Airlines (PIA), which was privatised through an auction in December last year. “The government is neither buying aircraft for a privatised PIA, nor has it announced any sovereign guarantee of taxpayer-funded loan for doing so,” Schehzad posted on X following claims on social media that a minister was arranging and negotiating sovereign-linked financing for the jets. The claims came after a recent meeting between Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb and Chair of the US Export-Import (Exim) Bank John Jovanovich on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. The finance ministry said about the meeting that the two discussed the Reko Diq mining project and funding opportunities for procuring an aircraft for PIA. The finance minister shared PIA’s interest in Boeing’s 787 Dreamliners and “sought support for a financing package covering aircraft and engines”. But, Schehzad pointed out in his post, the US Exim’s “mandate, like export credit agencies elsewhere, is to support its country’s exports and jobs”. “Boeing aircraft are US exports. US Exim provides financing support to foreign purchasers of US-manufactured aircraft, including airlines, through established financing structures. “US Exim’s own framework provides for asset-backed aircraft financing, where financing can be secured against the aircraft itself and credit assessed on the airline/lessee and/or guarantor, if any. A sovereign guarantee is therefore not an automatic requirement,” he added. Explaining the government’s role regarding the potential acquisition of the aircraft, he said it was doing “exactly what governments around the world are expected to do for their businesses: opening doors, facilitating access to international financing, technology and suppliers and promoting investment and commercial opportunities”. He added that Aurangzeb’s discussions with US Exim were not even confined to PIA. It covered potential financing across aviation, refinery upgrades and Reko Diq as part of a much broader Pakistan-US economic engagement. “And this is entirely consistent with Pakistan’s economic direction,” Schehzad remarked. He added that the government was “deliberately reducing the state’s role in commercial activity, pursuing privatisation and creating greater space for private capital. Private-sector-led growth does not mean government abandons the private sector; it means government enables it rather than running businesses itself”. “Therefore, claims of a ‘public loan, hidden subsidy, state backstop’ or taxpayers assuming PIA’s commercial risk should not be presented as facts when no such arrangement has been announced. The official statement refers to potential US Exim financing support; it does not announce government borrowing for PIA or a sovereign guarantee. “Privatisation transfers ownership and commercial management. It does not require the government of Pakistan to stop opening doors for Pakistani companies,” he said.

items.title: Dangote Refinery IPO: Northern Christian leader urges investment
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Chairman of the Northern Christian Association, NCA, Rev. Joseph John Hayab, has urged Christians across the country to participate in the ongoing Initial Public Offering, IPO, of Dangote Petroleum Refinery, saying religious considerations should not influence investment decisions. Hayab made the call on Saturday at a media parley in Kaduna, where he described the public offer as a business opportunity open to Nigerians irrespective of their religious affiliations. According to him, Christians should see the offer as an opportunity to acquire shares in a Nigerian company and build wealth for themselves, their families and future generations. “Business has no religion. What Dangote is selling is not Islam; Dangote is selling shares. Shares bring money,” he said. The Christian leader said responsible religious leaders should encourage their members to develop a culture of investment rather than relying solely on salaries and other regular sources of income. “If I have my way, just as they are advertising, every Christian should have 10 shares,” Hayab said. He argued that widespread participation by Nigerians in the offer could increase domestic ownership of businesses operating in the country and contribute to economic growth. Hayab also encouraged Christians to consider buying shares as part of long-term financial planning, including investments for the education and welfare of their children and grandchildren. “Buy it for your son. Buy it for your grandchildren. Buy it for the future of their education,” he said. He further linked investment culture to the financial capacity of churches, arguing that members who build sustainable wealth would be better positioned to support religious and community activities. “The reason why our offering is poor in many of our churches is because we are not investing,” he said, adding that many church members depended largely on salaries. The Dangote Petroleum Refinery public offer comprises 4.1 billion ordinary shares at ₦525 per share, with a minimum subscription of 10 shares valued at ₦5,250. The offer opened on September 14 and is scheduled to close on October 13, 2026. Hayab urged Nigerians to develop greater interest in owning stakes in businesses operating within the country, saying broader participation in investment would give citizens a stronger economic stake in the nation’s development. “The economy of Nigeria will grow faster if all Nigerians have a stake in the investment that is in Nigeria,” he said. items.description: Plus de 4 000 kits scolaires pour desserrer la contrainte financière de la rentrée : à Port-Gentil, Gabon Espoir et Génération Citoyenne reconduisent leur opération « École pour tous ». Cette troisième édition, lancée le 26 septembre, doit également bénéficier aux élèves du département de Bendjé. Un responsable de Gabon Espoir remettant des kits scolaires. © GabonReview La solidarité a pris rendez-vous dans les écoles de Port-Gentil, samedi 26 septembre. Les associations Gabon Espoir et Génération Citoyenne y ont entamé la troisième édition de l’opération « École pour tous », destinée aux enfants de familles modestes. Une première remise de fournitures au directeur de l’école de Quartier Sud 1, dans le quatrième arrondissement, a précédé la cérémonie organisée sur le plateau sportif de l’école publique de Matiti 1. © GabonReview Cette mobilisation répond aux difficultés que les familles font remonter aux organisateurs à chaque rentrée. Pour Raphaël Christian Pekoué, coordonnateur de Gabon Espoir dans le département de Bendjé, il s’agit d’apporter une contribution concrète, mais aussi d’anticiper les demandes d’aide. « Nous savons que toutes les familles n’ont pas les mêmes possibilités, les mêmes moyens pour faire partir les enfants à l’école » , souligne Jean de Dieu Nzigou, secrétaire général de Gabon Espoir. Créée en 2008, l’association inscrit ce rendez-vous de septembre dans son soutien aux foyers économiquement fragiles. Des fournitures, une exigence de travail À la remise des kits, les responsables associatifs ont associé un appel à l’assiduité. « Le meilleur investissement que l’on puisse faire pour son enfant, que le pays puisse faire pour ses enfants, c’est leur donner une éducation » , affirme Saturnin Aubame, président de Gabon Espoir. Aux élèves, il adresse une attente précise : « Nous attendons de vous simplement que vous fassiez preuve de discipline à l’école et que vous vous mettiez résolument au travail. » Parmi les parents présents, Noémie Omanda salue une aide qui complète les achats déjà effectués : « C’est une bonne chose de perpétuer ce genre d’initiative. Je félicite vraiment Gabon Espoir et Génération Citoyenne. » Selon le comité d’organisation, la distribution se poursuivra dans le département de Bendjé, auprès des élèves de l’école primaire de N’tchengué village et du canton Océan. items.title: COPSUN rejects two-year extension of UNIOSUN VC’s tenure
items.description: By Adeola Badru The Committee of Pro-Chancellors of State-Owned Universities, COPSUN, has urged Osun State Governor and Visitor to Osun State University, UNIOSUN, Ademola Adeleke, to halt what it described as the “illegal extension” of the tenure of the university’s Vice-Chancellor beyond the statutory five-year term. COPSUN also called for the National Universities Commission, NUC, to be legally strengthened and empowered to exercise overriding regulatory authority over university administration nationwide. The committee said professional regulatory bodies should be restricted to participating in NUC-led accreditation teams rather than conducting separate and overlapping regulatory exercises. The resolutions were contained in a communique issued at the end of COPSUN’s 73rd quarterly meeting and signed by its Chairman, Prof. Ayodeji Omole, and made available to journalists in Ibadan. On the UNIOSUN Vice-Chancellor’s tenure, COPSUN said it received a report that the Vice-Chancellor’s tenure had been extended by two years beyond the statutory five-year term through an executive pronouncement by the Visitor, with a proposal to amend the university’s law to legitimise the extension. The committee described the reported development as contrary to the existing legal framework governing the university. COPSUN resolved to formally notify Adeleke, as Visitor to the university, “regarding this illegality and the need to adhere strictly to the existing law of the University in line with the University Miscellaneous Act of 2012 as amended.” It also urged the university’s Pro-Chancellor, who is a member of COPSUN, to ensure strict adherence to the law and due process in order to protect the integrity of university governance. “The Pro Chancellor of the University, who is a member of COPSUN, is also urged to adhere to law and due process to safeguard the governance integrity of the university system,” the committee said. The committee’s position on UNIOSUN formed part of wider concerns over what it described as increasing interference by professional regulatory bodies in the administration and governance of Nigerian universities. COPSUN called on the NUC, as the regulatory authority for the university system, to take a more central role in university accreditation and regulation. It argued that professional bodies should participate as members of accreditation teams led by the NUC rather than independently subjecting universities to multiple regulatory exercises. The committee resolved that “the National Universities Commission (NUC), as the regulatory authority for the university system should be legally strengthened and empowered to exercise overriding authority over university administration nationwide with the professional bodies serving only as part of the accreditation team being headed by NUC”. COPSUN said the position followed reports received from various state-owned universities concerning what it described as growing interference by professional regulatory bodies in university governance. According to the committee, “COPSUN received the reports from our various universities over the growing interference of professional regulatory bodies in university governance. These organisations, though legally established and constitutionally empowered, subject universities to multiple overlapping exercises such as resource verification, accreditation, indexing, induction, and licensing.” “These acts put a lot of pressure on the universities, leading to accreditation fatigue in most universities’ systems,” it added. COPSUN maintained that centralising the accreditation process under the NUC, while retaining professional bodies within accreditation teams, would reduce the burden of multiple and overlapping regulatory exercises on universities and strengthen the coherence of the university system. items.title: Flamingos thrash Togo 4-0 to lift WAFU-B U-17 Girls Cup
items.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos have won the 2026 WAFU-B U-17 Girls Cup after completing a perfect campaign with a commanding 4-0 victory over Togo in Yamoussoukro, Côte d’Ivoire. The Flamingos finished the tournament unbeaten, recording five wins from five matches to underline their dominance throughout the competition. Captain Chidera Harmony was the star of the final, scoring twice from the penalty spot as Nigeria took a commanding lead before half-time. Harmony converted her first penalty in the 15th minute before doubling the advantage from another spot-kick 20 minutes later. Nigeria went into the break with a 2-0 lead and continued to control proceedings after the restart. Oluebube Umejiaku extended the Flamingos’ advantage in the 67th minute before Oluwakemi Adegbuyi completed the scoring in the 90th minute. The victory sealed Nigeria’s fifth consecutive win of the tournament and capped a dominant campaign characterised by attacking efficiency and defensive discipline. The title also provides a major boost for coach Hakeem Busari and his players as they continue preparations for the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco next month. The Flamingos, bronze medallists at the 2022 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, will now turn their attention to the global tournament. items.title: Nigeria targets 10m globally certified workers by 2030 — Alausa
items.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Government has unveiled plans to transform Nigeria’s youthful population into a globally competitive workforce, targeting 10 million globally certified Nigerians and one million export-linked jobs by 2030 under its National Talent Export Programme. The Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, disclosed this at the Hire From Nigeria side event held on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York. Alausa said the Federal Ministry of Education was repositioning the country’s education and skills system to produce trained, certified and adaptable workers capable of meeting the demands of the global outsourcing and digitally enabled services market. According to him, Nigeria’s large English-speaking youth population, cultural adaptability and growing digital capabilities provide a strong foundation for the country to compete for jobs and services in the global economy. “Nigeria’s greatest asset is its people: a young, ambitious, English-speaking and increasingly digitally capable population. Our task in Education is to turn that scale into verified competence and reliable service delivery,” he said. The minister said the global outsourcing and digitally enabled services economy offered Nigeria opportunities to create jobs, increase export earnings and enable citizens to build international careers without necessarily leaving the country. He, however, identified the disconnect between training and changing employer demands, inadequate work-based learning opportunities and limited access to internationally recognised certifications as major challenges requiring urgent attention. Alausa said the government was addressing the challenges through curriculum reforms, stronger accreditation and quality assurance, as well as expanded digital and technical training through federal institutions and credible private training providers. He stressed that employers must have a permanent role in shaping the skills pipeline, rather than being consulted only when curricula are due for periodic review. “We need a permanent employer-led feedback loop, not occasional curriculum reviews,” he said. Under the proposed model, employers would participate from programme design through training, assessment, certification and recruitment to ensure that graduates acquire skills that correspond directly with labour-market demands. Alausa also disclosed that the Federal Government’s free Technical and Vocational Education and Training, TVET, programme had attracted more than one million applications, with about 160,000 trainees already supported through approximately 1,200 centres nationwide. The centres include Federal Technical Colleges and accredited private training institutions. He said the government was also promoting multiple pathways into employment and enterprise, including university education, TVET, apprenticeships and continuous upskilling. According to him, the objective is to reposition skills acquisition as a direct route to employment, entrepreneurship, income generation and further learning, while changing perceptions about technical and vocational education. AI, digital skills take centre stage The minister said preparing Nigerian youths for an economy increasingly driven by artificial intelligence and advanced technologies was also at the heart of the education reform agenda. “We must train young people to work with artificial intelligence, not to compete with it on routine tasks,” Alausa said. He said future-ready workers would require skills that complement technology, including judgment, creativity, domain knowledge, data literacy, cybersecurity, cloud services, software development, customer success, quality assurance and AI-enabled operations. Through the Federal Government’s Digital Training Academy, he said partnerships with global learning providers, including Coursera and Pluralsight, were providing 32,000 Nigerians with free access to professional digital and technology training. The programme covers areas such as product management, cloud computing, cybersecurity, IT automation, artificial intelligence and machine learning, agentic AI, fintech, parallel and quantum computing, and natural language processing. The minister added that the Student Venture Capital Grant was supporting students in STEMM disciplines to convert innovative ideas into viable businesses, strengthening the link between education, innovation and enterprise. Alausa challenged international employers, Business Process Outsourcing, BPO, operators, investors and development partners to move beyond expressions of interest and build practical, investable talent pipelines in Nigeria. He urged employers to clearly define their skills requirements, co-design training programmes, provide work-based learning opportunities, recognise credible Nigerian certifications, recruit from Nigerian talent pools and provide feedback on workforce performance. BPO operators and investors, he said, should also establish and expand delivery centres beyond the country’s major commercial cities while investing in training infrastructure, connectivity, quality systems and management capacity. Development partners, he added, could support the initiative through scalable certification programmes, instructor development, inclusion of women and underserved communities, labour-market intelligence and systems for measuring employment outcomes rather than merely counting trainees. He also called for stronger international institutional partnerships and centres of excellence in Nigerian institutions to deepen global linkages, benchmarking and knowledge transfer. Alausa said the ministry would, in return, deepen industry participation in curriculum development and certification, expand market-relevant TVET and digital-skills pathways, strengthen accreditation and quality assurance, and improve the link between educational institutions, training providers and employers. The initiatives form part of the ministry’s role on the supply side of the National Talent Export Programme, under which Nigeria is targeting one million export-linked jobs and 10 million globally certified Nigerians by 2030. The Federal Ministry of Education is also leading the programme’s Supply Technical Working Group. Alausa said the reforms were aligned with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, particularly its focus on human capital development, job creation, skills acquisition and inclusive economic growth. “Under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, our commitment is clear: we will continue to invest in the skills, knowledge and innovation of our young people and build an education system that gives Nigerian talent the capacity and confidence to compete and succeed anywhere in the world,” he said. He said the ultimate goal was to build an education and skills system capable of connecting Nigerian talent to global opportunities while strengthening the country’s position in the international economy and enabling more young Nigerians to build sustainable careers at home and abroad. items.title: KiDi brings the hits to London in sold-out UK headline concert
items.description: Ghanaian singer KiDi has made a strong mark in London with a sold-out performance at his first-ever UK solo headline concert. Held at Outernet Live, London, the concert brought together fans who sang, danced and cheered their way through a night of KiDi’s biggest hits and songs from his latest album, Where Do We Go From Here . The concert formed part of the rollout for the album and gave KiDi the opportunity to take his latest body of work directly to his international audience. From the opening moments, the packed venue was filled with energy as the singer moved through a selection of fan favourites, with the crowd joining him word-for-word on several of his popular songs. KiDi performed hits alongside songs from Where Do We Go From Here . Videos from the concert shared on social media showed fans dancing throughout the performance and responding enthusiastically to the singer’s set. The event also featured performances from Tanzanian star Harmonize, Compozers and rapper Flowking Stone. OgeeTheMC hosted the show, while dance performances by Dancegod Loyd added to the night’s entertainment. The sold-out London concert represents a new milestone for KiDi, marking his first solo headline show in the United Kingdom as he continues to take his music to audiences beyond Ghana. It also adds momentum to the promotion of Where Do We Go From Here , his latest album, as the award-winning musician continues to build his international audience.

items.title: «Mu Tsanu», 640 établissements : le pari scolaire d’Annie-Flore Batchiellilys
items.description: Faire de l’écoute et du dialogue des réflexes dès l’école : c’est l’ambition d’Annie-Flore Batchiellilys avec « Mu Tsanu », une tournée nationale annoncée à partir du 15 novembre. À la croisée de la musique et de la médiation professionnelle, l’artiste gabonaise prévoit de toucher 640 établissements scolaires et quelque 6 400 personnes pour apprendre à mieux communiquer, prévenir les conflits et renouer le dialogue. Avec «Mu Tsanu», Annie-Flore Batchiellilys veut faire résonner le dialogue dans les écoles, à la croisée de la musique et de la médiation. © institutfrancais-gabon Avec « Mu Tsanu », qui signifie « la relation » en langue ipunu, Annie-Flore Batchiellilys entend porter son engagement sur le terrain scolaire. La tournée doit réunir élèves, personnels de l’éducation et associations de parents d’élèves autour d’ateliers consacrés à la communication, à l’écoute, au dialogue et à la gestion des relations. Le projet repose sur la complémentarité de deux univers qui structurent aujourd’hui le parcours de l’artiste : la musique et la médiation professionnelle. La première offre un moyen d’expression et de transmission ; la seconde doit aider à dénouer les situations conflictuelles et à rechercher des solutions par le dialogue. « Mu Tsanu » ambitionne ainsi d’amener les communautés scolaires à explorer « une autre manière d’être, de communiquer, de nous écouter et de vivre les uns avec les autres ». Pour l’artiste, la qualité des relations humaines est une condition essentielle à un environnement éducatif plus apaisé. Dans le prolongement de Mighoma Cette initiative s’inscrit dans la continuité des engagements d’Annie-Flore Batchiellilys en faveur de la transmission culturelle et du lien social. En janvier 2025, elle avait inauguré à Akanda, au nord de Libreville, le Centre culturel Mighoma. Pensé comme un lieu de création et de rencontres entre générations, l’espace devait notamment accueillir des activités autour des langues traditionnelles, des instruments et danses du Gabon, des contes et des jeux traditionnels. Quelques mois plus tard, en septembre 2025, l’artiste annonçait cependant la fermeture du centre, invoquant notamment des difficultés financières et des charges de fonctionnement devenues trop lourdes. De la scène à la médiation Avant cette nouvelle initiative, Annie-Flore Batchiellilys avait également élargi son activité à la médiation professionnelle en créant Muleby, un cabinet spécialisé dans ce domaine et le conseil. Après plus de trois décennies consacrées à la musique, l’artiste expliquait, dès 2022, avoir choisi de se former à la médiation pour contribuer à prévenir l’escalade des conflits et à favoriser le règlement des différends. Avec « Mu Tsanu », ces expériences convergent vers un même objectif : mettre la musique, la transmission culturelle et la médiation au service du dialogue dans les communautés scolaires. La tournée doit sillonner le territoire national à partir du 15 novembre. À travers cette démarche, Annie-Flore Batchiellilys entend faire de l’écoute une pratique partagée et du dialogue un moyen de retisser les liens. Une ambition résumée par sa conviction : « la restauration de la relation commence par nous ». items.title: Sebta : Madrid veut accélérer le retour des migrants
items.description: Confronté à des milliers de dossiers encore en suspens depuis la vague migratoire des 30 et 31 juillet à Sebta, le gouvernement de Pedro Sánchez prépare un décret-loi exceptionnel destiné à accélérer les procédures de retour des migrants arrivés dans la ville lors de cette crise. Selon El País, le texte, dont la présentation est envisagée mardi prochain, doit permettre aux autorités espagnoles de raccourcir les procédures liées aux opérations de retour et d’éloignement. Une disposition particulièrement sensible prévoit notamment la possibilité de renvoyer certains demandeurs d’asile avant l’épuisement de toutes les voies de recours, leurs dossiers pouvant continuer à être examinés après leur départ d’Espagne. Le projet intervient alors que Madrid cherche à résorber l’engorgement administratif provoqué par l’ampleur des arrivées enregistrées durant la vague de juillet. Plus de dix mille migrants seraient encore présents à Sebta, selon les chiffres relayés par la presse espagnole, tandis que les autorités peinent à traiter les dossiers dans les délais habituels. Une mesure qui divise le gouvernement L’initiative ne fait toutefois pas consensus au sein de la coalition gouvernementale. Le parti Sumar s’oppose notamment au renvoi de demandeurs d’asile avant qu’une décision définitive ne soit rendue sur leur situation. À l’inverse, le Parti populaire, dans l’opposition, réclame une accélération des procédures de retour. Le gouvernement espagnol se retrouve ainsi confronté à un double impératif : réduire la pression exercée sur les capacités d’accueil de Sebta tout en respectant les garanties prévues par le droit d’asile et les procédures de recours. Le recours à un décret-loi exceptionnel traduit l’urgence avec laquelle Madrid entend traiter cette situation. Son adoption mardi reste toutefois incertaine, selon les informations disponibles. Plus de 7.500 retours depuis août Les opérations de retour ont déjà commencé, mais elles concernent pour l’essentiel des personnes arrivées avant la crise de juillet. Le ministre espagnol de la Politique territoriale et de la Mémoire démocratique, Ángel Víctor Torres, a indiqué jeudi dernier que 7.533 migrants avaient regagné le Maroc à partir de Sebta depuis le début du mois d’août. Parmi eux, 7.099 sont repartis volontairement, tandis que 364 ont fait l’objet de procédures d’éloignement, a-t-il précisé. Cette dernière catégorie concerne des personnes entrées dans la ville avant la vague des 30 et 31 juillet. Les procédures visant les migrants arrivés pendant cette période n’ont, elles, pas encore été finalisées. C’est précisément ce retard que le gouvernement cherche désormais à résorber. D’après les données relayées par plusieurs médias espagnols, l’examen des dossiers liés à la crise de juillet peut prendre jusqu’à douze semaines. Dans le même temps, de nouveaux dossiers continuent d’être ouverts à un rythme compris entre 30 et 50 % par semaine. Le Maroc au centre du dispositif de retour La coopération avec Rabat reste centrale dans ce dispositif. Les autorités marocaines ont fait savoir qu’elles étaient disposées à coopérer au retour des personnes qui ne remplissent pas les conditions pour bénéficier d’une protection internationale. Cette coopération intervient dans un contexte où la gestion de la frontière et des retours constitue depuis plusieurs années un volet important du partenariat migratoire entre le Maroc et l’Espagne. Madrid bénéficie également d’un soutien financier européen. La Commission européenne a prévu une enveloppe de 114,7 millions d’euros pour contribuer à la gestion de la crise à Sebta et soutenir notamment les opérations de retour et le renforcement des capacités de contrôle. Mais l’enjeu dépasse désormais la seule question du contrôle frontalier. Pour l’Espagne, il s’agit de trouver un mécanisme permettant de traiter rapidement les milliers de situations individuelles héritées de la crise de juillet, sans ouvrir un nouveau front juridique autour du droit d’asile. La décision attendue mardi pourrait donc constituer une étape importante dans la gestion de cette problématique.
